title: Ang 1186–1187: the ninth Guru in Basant
tomorrow: a saint grinds sandalwood for the temple. why does he stay home?

cards: Some elevators skip the thirteenth floor: twelve, then fourteen, and nobody explains. Basant has its own skipped floors. The headings have been climbing: Mahala 1, Guru Nanak; Mahala 3, Mahala 4, Mahala 5.
Then, on ang 1186, the next heading says Mahala 9. No six, no seven, no eight. A kid at a Sikh summer camp spotted it this week and asked the obvious question.

teach.h: THE FIRST FIVE, AND THE NINTH.
teach.b: Nothing fell out. The Granth holds hymns from the first five Gurus and from the ninth, and none from the sixth, seventh or eighth. Check any raga where the ninth Guru sings: the headings jump the same way.

teach.h: A SON ADDS HIS FATHER'S HYMNS.
teach.b: Tradition says the tenth Guru, Guru Gobind Singh, added his father's hymns, the hymns of Guru Tegh Bahadur, the ninth, to the Granth. So the jump isn't a gap. It's a family.
A son placing his father's voice beside the Gurus before him, and the father signing, like all of them, as Nanak. Now the second odd thing.
This is the spring raga, full of blossoms, and the ninth Guru's voice is spare, almost wintry.
In paraphrase: saadho, holy one, know this body as passing.
The Lord who lives within it, know that one as true. In the middle of all that blooming, he points at the body and says: this, too, is a season. Not to spoil the spring, but to show what's under it.
The flowers come and go; the One living in the body stays. Something to tell a friend tonight: open the Granth anywhere, and if you see Mahala 9, you're hearing the father of the tenth Guru.
The ninth: the floor that's there after the skip.

how: Readers find Guru Tegh Bahadur's hymns by the heading Mahala 9, right after Guru Arjan's in each raga where he wrote; ragis sing them in kirtan.

practice: Rest one hand flat on your chest and find your heartbeat. Feel the body doing its work, this season of it, without your help. Under it, the ninth Guru says, is the One that stays.
If you'd like, read ang 1186 before you begin.
